scope.role: Select/review data-access patterns based on domain, access ownership and object/schema coupling; preserve simple gateways and directly mapped JPA entities as legitimate choices.
reviewCriteria: Trace authority over state, callers, schema ownership, actual reads and writes, transaction scope and isolation.
Separate mapping independence from concurrency guarantees; avoid mapper migration as an unsupported fix.
Preserve read-projection/write-intent protections, optimistic tokens, effective mixed JDBC/JPA participation and partial-example limits.
Compare the smallest sufficient change and no change; keep detailed concurrency protocols with existing neighboring owners.
scope.procedure: Read complete review prompt, wave4 brief and entire assigned package; reviewed coordinator baseline row and actual scoped Git state. Reused unchanged skill-engineering and parallel-review instructions/readings. Findings delivered before editing; no ownership conflict.

versions.rationale: One patch for focused pattern-selection/concurrency-boundary guidance and verified source-link repairs. No description, dependency or technology-baseline change.

baseline.coordinatorBaseline: docs/skill-validation/wave4-2026-10-16/baseline.json: data-source-patterns row matched assignment hashes and versions.

findings.finding: Existing guidance protected loaded entity versions but did not explicitly bound those protections when a decision reads multiple rows and writes different rows. The pattern-selection workflow could leave a missing isolation/concurrency protocol misattributed to missing mapping.
findings.consequence: A mapper or unit-of-work migration can preserve the same invalid cross-row interleaving. This is a supported missing decision boundary, not a measured agent failure.
changes: Trace the rule read set, write predicates, participating writers and effective isolation/transaction boundary.
Explain the independently versioned-row counterexample and preserve narrow guarded SQL or simple mappers when sufficient.
Route protocol selection to enterprise-transactions/offline-concurrency-control, which were already declared in suggests.

findings.finding: Two distinct Jakarta source URLs, appearing three times, returned HTTP 404.
findings.consequence: Readers could not consult the referenced merge/version or EntityManager contracts.
findings.evidence: Direct HEAD checks: old URLs 404; corrected URLs 200; GET source snapshots retained.

capabilitiesPreserved: All four pattern definitions and classification by responsibility rather than class/table names.
Schema/domain-shape ownership, simple mapper/Active Record/gateway alternatives and module-level coexistence.
Mapping identity and expected version preservation; lifecycle reconstitution and pure rule-test distinctions.
Read projections remain separate from writable state; omission/null/merge semantics and conditional narrow updates.
Shared JDBC/JPA transaction participation, flush-versus-commit, managed-state reconciliation and bulk/version caveats.
Java 17 and Spring 6.1+ partial-example baseline, unchanged descriptions/dependencies/referrals.
All five Java fenced snippets remained byte-for-byte identical.

@@ -110,6 +110,30 @@ state. Reconstitution must reject corrupt combinations or translate known legacy
 explicitly; it is not permission to bypass all validation. Use an appropriately accessible
 factory without weakening creation invariants.
 
+### Concurrency scope is separate from mapping style
+
+The version check above protects the entity being written; it does not automatically validate
+every other row read to make that decision. Suppose a rule requires at least one available
+operator. Two transactions both read two available operators, then each disables a different
+operator using that row's unchanged version. Both row-version checks can succeed under isolation
+that permits this interleaving. Moving the same reads and writes behind a mapper, or collecting
+them in a unit of work, does not remove the race.
+
+Inspect the rule's read set, actual write predicates, participating writers and effective
+database isolation/lock modes. Keep a narrow conditional update or simple mapper when its
+guard covers the required state. If the rule spans independently updated rows, choose a
+protocol covering that state rather than adding a second object model as a concurrency fix.
+Shared version/locking protocols or serializable transactions with whole-transaction retry
+may be candidates; their scope, costs and interaction with other writers need validation.
+Use `enterprise-transactions` and `offline-concurrency-control` for that choice. Test a
+controlled two-transaction interleaving as well as the legitimate rule that allows both writes.
+
+Jakarta Persistence 3.1 section 3.4 scopes version checks to entity state and leaves database
+isolation configuration outside the specification. As one database-specific example,
+[PostgreSQL 17 isolation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/transaction-iso.html) permits
+serialization anomalies at Read Committed and Repeatable Read. Verify the actual database;
+an ORM transaction annotation or isolation-level name alone is not proof of the needed guarantee.
+

sources.scope: Jakarta Persistence 3.1, sections 3.4/3.4.1/3.4.2 and footnote 31; entity-level version checks and isolation configuration.
Jakarta Persistence 3.1 EntityManager flush/clear/refresh contracts; repair source navigation.

Fowler Unit of Work: change coordination; pattern responsibility does not select a concrete database isolation protocol.
